data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy that defines the roles and responsibilities of the Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officers (TMACO).
policy_statements.target: roles and responsibilities of the Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officers (TMACO)

policy_statements.source_text: This DR also delineates the level of collaboration and involvement of the TMACOs in the planning, acquisition, deployment, management, and disposition of information technology (IT) investments for telecommunications services, equipment, facilities, and resources.
policy_statements.target: level of collaboration and involvement of the TMACOs

policy_statements.source_text: This DR updates and revises TMACO roles and responsibilities related to management of all data, voice, wireless, and other telecommunication products and services.
This regulation supersedes DR 3300-020, Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officer (TMACO) - Roles and Responsibilities, dated October 13, 2016.
cross_references: DR 3300-020, Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officer (TMACO) - Roles and Responsibilities, dated October 13, 2016

policy_statements.source_text: This DR will be in effect until superseded or the expiration date.
conditions: until superseded or the expiration date

policy_statements.source_text: The term “agency” or phrase “agency and staff office,” unless otherwise noted in this directive, will be considered to encompass the Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices of USDA.
conditions: unless otherwise noted in this directive

policy_statements.source_text: All agencies and staff offices will align their policies and procedures with this DR within 6 months of the publication date.
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: All agencies and staff offices may supplement this DR when developing their internal guidance.
Modifications to the intent or purpose of this DR are not allowed.
policy_statements.target: intent or purpose of this DR

policy_statements.source_text: If agencies and staff offices publish internal guidance that supplements this DR, one copy of each supplement will be forwarded to the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), Digital Infrastructure Services Center (DISC), Enterprise Network Services (ENS), Telecommunications Infrastructure Management and Governance (TIMG) at ens.policy@ocio.usda.gov.
conditions: If agencies and staff offices publish internal guidance that supplements this DR

policy_statements.source_text: In June 1998, the Government Accountability Office (GAO) issued an audit report, GAO/AIMD-98-131, USDA Telecommunications: Strong Leadership Needed to Resolve Management Weaknesses, Achieve Savings, that reiterated the need for USDA to address its telecommunications management practices.
cross_references: GAO/AIMD-98-131, USDA Telecommunications: Strong Leadership Needed to Resolve Management Weaknesses, Achieve Savings

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) directed the agencies and staff offices to establish the TMACO role in response to this audit.
The TMACOs serve as the agency or staff office single point of contact (POC) for telecommunications services to ensure compliance with Departmental telecommunications requirements and guidance.
This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices.
policy_statements.target: all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: USDA agencies and staff offices will support all Departmental and Federal laws, regulations, policies, and initiatives for streamlining, consolidating, and achieving cost savings related to the planning, acquisition, deployment, management, and disposition of IT investments for telecommunications services, equipment, facilities, and resources in accordance with DR-3300-001, Telecommunications & Internet Services and Use.
policy_statements.target: all Departmental and Federal laws, regulations, policies, and initiatives
cross_references: DR-3300-001, Telecommunications & Internet Services and Use

policy_statements.source_text: TMACOs will have demonstrated knowledge and experience with telecommunications and IT for acquisition development and management, policies, practices, services and technologies, financial and inventory management processes, ordering and billing methodologies, and automated telecommunication enterprise management tools.
policy_statements.target: demonstrated knowledge and experience with telecommunications and IT

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA CIO will:

Work with Mission Area Assistant CIOs and agency and staff office IT Directors to formulate and communicate vision, business values, goals, and objectives for telecommunications management in USDA; and
policy_statements.target: vision, business values, goals, and objectives for telecommunications management in USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure the overall TMACO program objectives are aligned and integrated with the General Services Administration (GSA) Federal Strategic Sourcing Initiative (FSSI), direction from the Federal CIO, and the current USDA Information Technology Strategic Plan.
cross_references: General Services Administration (GSA) Federal Strategic Sourcing Initiative (FSSI)

policy_statements.source_text: Perform management and/or oversight responsibilities in accordance with the Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291, as applicable to this directive.
cross_references: Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291

policy_statements.source_text: The ENS Director will:
Develop policy guidance to formally establish the TMACO Program and define the roles and responsibilities for agency and staff office TMACOs;
Ensure that a formal organization structure and resources are in place to support the TMACO Program goals and objectives;
Ensure that a governance program is in place that measures agency and staff office compliance against stated goals, objectives, and key performance indicators;
Ensure agency and staff office compliance with all applicable Federal mandates and related Departmental regulations and guidance;
Establish the roles and responsibilities for the TMACO position;
policy_statements.target: roles and responsibilities for the TMACO position

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that all agency and staff office TMACOs attain certification as a Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) representative through the Federal Acquisition Certification Contracting Officer's Representative (FAC-COR) training program, if not already certified.
policy_statements.target: all agency and staff office TMACOs
cross_references: Federal Acquisition Certification Contracting Officer's Representative (FAC-COR) training program

policy_statements.source_text: TMACOs must take the FAC-COR training every 2 years to maintain their certification;
Provide agency and staff office personnel responsible for telecommunications services with access to the USDA enterprise telecommunications expense management tool and vendor portals;
policy_statements.target: agency and staff office personnel responsible for telecommunications services

policy_statements.source_text: Develop enterprise tools and processes for reviewing agency and staff office ordering, usage, and billing of telecommunications services to ensure compliance with Departmental policies and guidelines to avoid fraud, waste, and abuse;
Develop and maintain the TMACOs quarterly savings reports.
Combine agency and staff office savings reports to create a USDA total savings report;
policy_statements.target: agency and staff office savings reports

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with agencies and staff offices to compile submissions for Departmental and Federal data calls within the specified timeframes; and
policy_statements.target: submissions for Departmental and Federal data calls

policy_statements.source_text: Provide a TMACO Program report that consists of cost savings and optimization services to Mission Area Assistant CIOs, agency and staff office IT Directors, and TMACOs twice a year.
Mission Area Assistant CIOs, and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors will:
Ensure agency and staff office employees comply with this directive;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs, and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure agency and staff office internal directives conform to this DR’s stated requirements;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs, and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors
policy_statements.target: agency and staff office internal directives

policy_statements.source_text: Engage TMACOs in the formulation of goals and objectives for the TMACO program;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs, and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Appoint personnel to serve in the agency and staff office TMACO role;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs, and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Establish communication channels with the agency or staff office TMACO and designated budget personnel;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs, and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that TMACOs perform required telecommunications expense management activities such as billing and inventory validation and cost savings tracking, using telecommunications management tools; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs, and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that agency and staff office TMACOs compile submissions for Departmental and Federal data calls within the specified timeframes.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs, and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs will:
Serve as the agency or staff office single POC for telecommunications services to ensure compliance with Departmental telecommunications requirements and guidance;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs

policy_statements.source_text: Use enterprise tools and processes to order, maintain, and manage a comprehensive inventory of telecommunication devices, equipment, services, costs, trending, and forecasting;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs
policy_statements.target: comprehensive inventory of telecommunication devices, equipment, services, costs, trending, and forecasting

policy_statements.source_text: Use tools and enterprise processes to validate telecommunications billing, inventory, and services.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs

policy_statements.source_text: On a quarterly basis, submit acknowledgement of validation and a report of any cost savings resulting from clean-up or optimization efforts to OCIO, DISC, ENS, TIMG.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs
policy_statements.target: acknowledgement of validation and a report of any cost savings resulting from clean-up or optimization efforts

policy_statements.source_text: Manage access to all telecommunications vendor business support systems for delegated staff within their agency or staff office;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs
policy_statements.target: all telecommunications vendor business support systems
conditions: for delegated staff within their agency or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: Provide agency and staff office personnel responsible for telecommunications services with enterprise management tool and vendor portal training;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs
policy_statements.target: agency and staff office personnel responsible for telecommunications services

policy_statements.source_text: Participate regularly in TMACO meetings and working groups;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with appropriate agency and staff office personnel at least annually to obligate funds for telecommunications charges within the specified timeframe;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs

policy_statements.source_text: Use tools and enterprise processes for reviewing agency and staff office ordering, usage, and billing of telecommunications services to ensure compliance with Departmental policies and guidelines to avoid fraud, waste, and abuse;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs
policy_statements.target: agency and staff office ordering, usage, and billing of telecommunications services

policy_statements.source_text: Communicate and disseminate Federal and Departmental information to agencies or staff offices regarding planning, acquisition, management, and disposition of investments for IT and telecommunications services, equipment, and resources within USDA;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs

policy_statements.source_text: Provide guidance to agencies and staff offices for the development of telecommunications and IT acquisitions;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs

policy_statements.source_text: Participate in Departmental IT and telecommunications projects to implement cost effective and streamlined enterprise solutions;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with telecommunications vendors (e.g., data, voice, and wireless) or telecommunications equipment manufacturers to obtain technology solutions for agencies and staff offices;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs
policy_statements.target: telecommunications vendors (e.g., data, voice, and wireless) or telecommunications equipment manufacturers

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with OCIO ENS to compile submissions for Departmental and Federal data calls within the specified timeframes; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs
policy_statements.target: submissions for Departmental and Federal data calls

policy_statements.source_text: Attain certification as a COR through the FAC-COR program, if not already certified.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office TMACOs

policy_statements.source_text: DR 4070-735-001, Employee Responsibilities and Conduct, Section 16 sets forth USDA’s policies, procedures, and standards on employee responsibilities and conduct relative to the use of computers and telecommunications equipment.
policy_statements.target: USDA’s policies, procedures, and standards on employee responsibilities and conduct relative to the use of computers and telecommunications equipment
cross_references: DR 4070-735-001, Employee Responsibilities and Conduct, Section 16

policy_statements.source_text: DR 4070-735-001, Section 21, states:
A violation of any of the responsibilities and conduct standards contained in this directive may be cause for disciplinary or adverse action; and
Disciplinary or adverse action will be effected in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Such disciplinary or adverse action will be effected in accordance with applicable laws and regulations such as Office of Personnel Management (OPM) regulations, Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regulations, and the Standards of Ethical Conduct for Employees of the Executive Branch.
cross_references: Standards of Ethical Conduct for Employees of the Executive Branch

This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy that defines the roles and responsibilities of the Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officers (TMACO). In June 1998, the Government Accountability Office (GAO) issued an audit report,  GAO/AIMD-98-131 , *USDA Telecommunications: Strong Leadership Needed to Resolve Management Weaknesses, Achieve Savings*, that reiterated the need for USDA to address its telecommunications management practices. The USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) directed the agencies and staff offices to establish the TMACO role in response to this audit. The TMACOs serve as the agency or staff office single point of contact (POC) for telecommunications services to ensure compliance with Departmental telecommunications requirements and guidance.

Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officer (TMACO) - Roles and Responsibilities
This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices.

a. This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy that defines the roles and responsibilities of the Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officers (TMACO). This DR also delineates the level of collaboration and involvement of the TMACOs in the planning, acquisition, deployment, management, and disposition of information technology (IT) investments for telecommunications services, equipment, facilities, and resources.
